messages:
alex.k: quick RFC follow-up — we need a concrete plan for service principals + token lifetimes. the RFC left the defaults vague
priya: agree. we should decide short-lived default + an escape hatch for long-lived keys for infra ops.
sam_g: +1. proposed defaults: api keys = long-lived but revocable, service tokens = short-lived (15m) with refresh via OIDC exchange.
miguel: why keep long-lived API keys at all? they’re a big attack surface. can we force rotate to short-lived for all new keys?
alex.k: legacy customers will push back. proposal: new keys -> short-lived only. existing keys get a migration window (90d). ops can request long-lived with justification and rotation policy.
dina: what about RBAC scoping? current model has org-level roles and project-level roles. do we allow service principals to be bound at org scope?
priya: my view: prefer project-scoped bindings for service principals by default. org-scope only for infra/system principals with extra approval flow. reduces blast radius. :lock:
sam_g: sounds good. need to handle cross-project jobs — recommend service principal with explicit list of project memberships instead of org-wide.
miguel: technical note: for short-lived tokens we should support token exchange (client gets a short-lived session via OIDC with audience=redwood, then exchange for a service token tied to a principal + allowed projects). keeps KMS/HSM signing centralized.
alex.k: +1. include audit log events: token.issue, token.exchange, role.bind, role.revoke. must log principal id, bound projects, requester id.
dina: example policy for clarity:
```json
{
  "principal": "svc-data-processor",
  "roles": ["project.viewer", "project.embedding_writer"],
  "projects": ["proj-analytics", "proj-features"],
  "token_ttl": "15m",
  "issued_by": "oidc-exchange"
}
```
priya: love the example. question: how to handle long-running batch jobs that legitimately need >15m?
sam_g: two options: 1) allow workload identity where job uses node identity to request a bound token scoped to that job with limited lifetime but auto-refresh via the runtime, 2) allow ephemeral long-lived tokens via an attestation flow (e.g., signed SAML/CI token) with stricter audit/rotation. prefer option 1.
miguel: implementation detail: runtime should cache a token per principal+project combo and re-use while respecting TTL, but we must avoid global caches that survive principal revocation. cache should check revocation feed.
alex.k: good callout. revocation: we will publish a revocation list + sequence number and require tokens to include seq at mint; servers check seq on validate.
dina: migration plan draft: 1) telemetry + inventory of long-lived keys, 2) opt-in short-lived for new keys, 3) 90d warning + auto-rotate via tooling, 4) org-scope deprecation unless approved.
priya: who owns the approval flow for org-scope? I volunteer security to own policy + audit, infra to own enforcement.
sam_g: need an SDK change too — expose token-exchange helper, transparent refresh, and a way to attach principal metadata when creating tokens. put it in the 2.1 SDK milestone.
miguel: one more tradeoff: how strict should RBAC be with resource-level perms (dataset/file) vs project-level? fine-grained is safer but costs eval time. propose project-level for v1, per-resource in v2 behind an opt-in flag.
alex.k: summary action items: priya + miguel write enforcement + revocation spec; sam_g + dina draft migration + SDK changes; i'll sync with product on org-scope approval UI. will follow up with a short RFC addendum. thanks all :thumbsup:
